questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: After Rome fell, medieval kingdoms in Western Europe became fragmented rather than unified. What was the main reason for this fragmentation?
options: There was no strong central authority to enforce law and collect taxes across large areas
The Catholic Church banned the formation of large kingdoms
The climate became too harsh for large armies to travel
Viking invasions destroyed all written records of Roman government
questions.answer: There was no strong central authority to enforce law and collect taxes across large areas
questions.why: Without Rome's centralised government, army, and tax system, power fell to local strongmen who could actually defend their land — leading to the fragmented, localised power of feudalism rather than one big kingdom.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A common mistake is thinking knights owned the land they fought on. In the feudal pyramid, what was the real relationship between a knight and their land?
options: Knights held land on loan from a lord in exchange for military service, they did not own it outright
Knights owned their land permanently and passed it to their children with no obligations
Knights rented their land from peasants for a fixed fee
Knights had no land at all and lived entirely off the king's treasury
questions.answer: Knights held land on loan from a lord in exchange for military service, they did not own it outright
questions.why: Feudal land (a fief) was granted conditionally — the knight (a vassal) owed military service in return, and the land could be reclaimed. This is different from modern outright ownership.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Romeo and Juliet was written in which broad time period of English history?
options: The Elizabethan era (late 1500s)
The Victorian era (1800s)
The medieval era (1200s)
The Georgian era (1700s)
questions.why: Shakespeare wrote during the reign of Elizabeth I, in the late 16th century — this is called the Elizabethan era, and it shaped the play's language and staging conventions.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In the prologue, the Chorus calls Romeo and Juliet 'star-crossed lovers.' A student says this just means 'unlucky in love.' What is this phrase actually foreshadowing?
options: That fate itself, not just bad luck, is set against them and dooms them from the start
That they are lucky because the stars favour young love
That they will become famous astronomers
That their families will forgive them because of the stars' influence
questions.answer: That fate itself, not just bad luck, is set against them and dooms them from the start
questions.why: 'Star-crossed' invokes the idea that the stars (fate/destiny) are actively working against the lovers — this is stronger than ordinary bad luck, and sets up the play's theme of fate versus free will.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Some students think the 'love vs hate' theme in Romeo and Juliet is only about romantic love. What does the theme actually explore?
options: How intense love and intense hate (like the family feud) are shown as closely linked forces that both lead to destruction
Only the romantic love between Romeo and Juliet, with no connection to the feud
How love always defeats hate by the end of the play
How hate is portrayed as a stronger emotion than love throughout
questions.answer: How intense love and intense hate (like the family feud) are shown as closely linked forces that both lead to destruction
questions.why: Shakespeare deliberately pairs love and hate throughout the play (e.g. 'loving hate') to show they are intertwined extremes — both the Capulet-Montague hatred and the lovers' passion drive the tragedy.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In an experiment testing how the amount of sunlight affects plant growth, what is the independent variable?
options: The amount of sunlight given to each plant
The height of the plant measured at the end
The type of soil used for all plants
The amount of water given to each plant
questions.answer: The amount of sunlight given to each plant
questions.why: The independent variable is the one the experimenter deliberately changes (sunlight amount) to see its effect on the dependent variable (plant growth) — it's the 'cause' being tested, not the outcome.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student says 'all animals reproduce sexually.' Which of these organisms is a clear counterexample, reproducing asexually instead?
options: Bacteria, which reproduce by binary fission without a mate
Humans, who require two parents
Elephants, who require two parents
Wolves, who require two parents
questions.answer: Bacteria, which reproduce by binary fission without a mate
questions.why: Bacteria reproduce asexually via binary fission, splitting into two identical cells with no need for a mate — this shows not all organisms need two parents to reproduce, unlike mammals.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A student claims the First Crusade was purely a religious mission with no political motives at all. What does this overlook?
options: European nobles and the Church also saw the Crusade as a chance to gain land, wealth, and political power
The Crusade had no religious motive at all, only political ones
The Pope had no involvement in organising the Crusade
European nobles refused to participate for any reason other than faith
questions.answer: European nobles and the Church also saw the Crusade as a chance to gain land, wealth, and political power
questions.why: While religious motivation was real and strongly promoted, the Crusades also offered nobles opportunities for land, titles, and wealth, and the Church gained influence — political and religious motives were intertwined, not separate.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A student says that after Rome fell, 'civilisation basically disappeared' in Western Europe. What is misleading about this claim?
options: Society continued and reorganised around the Church, local lords, and feudalism, rather than vanishing entirely
It's accurate — literacy, government, and society completely ceased to exist
Rome's fall had no lasting effects on Europe at all
Feudalism only began centuries later, so there was a total gap in society
questions.answer: Society continued and reorganised around the Church, local lords, and feudalism, rather than vanishing entirely
questions.why: Rome's collapse changed the structure of society dramatically (smaller, local, less centralised) but did not erase civilisation — the Church preserved learning, and feudal structures organised communities and defence.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Someone claims Romeo and Juliet was originally written as a novel and later adapted into a play. What is wrong with this claim?
options: It was written by Shakespeare as a stage play from the start, intended for performance at the Globe-era theatres
It was originally a Roman epic poem translated into English
It was first written as a film script in the 1500s
It was originally an opera composed for the royal court
questions.answer: It was written by Shakespeare as a stage play from the start, intended for performance at the Globe-era theatres
questions.why: Romeo and Juliet was composed as a play for live theatrical performance in Elizabethan London, not adapted from another format — this reflects Shakespeare's role as a working playwright of his era.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: A student says Juliet's line 'What's in a name? That which we call a rose by any other name would smell as sweet' is just a random observation about flowers. What is it actually doing?
options: Using a metaphor to argue that names (like 'Montague') are meaningless labels that shouldn't determine Romeo's true worth or their love
Literally teaching the audience facts about rose gardening
Showing Juliet's plan to grow roses to win over the Capulets
Foreshadowing that Romeo will give Juliet a rose as a gift
questions.answer: Using a metaphor to argue that names (like 'Montague') are meaningless labels that shouldn't determine Romeo's true worth or their love
questions.why: This is a key metaphor: Juliet argues that a name is just a label, disconnected from a person's true nature — directly challenging the feud that keeps her and Romeo apart because of their family names.

questions.prompt: Explain why historians often say the Crusades reshaped Europe's economy and worldview, even though the religious goal of holding Jerusalem ultimately failed. Use at least one specific effect that had nothing to do with military victory.
